issues.failure_explanation: In the regime used in the proof (sigma_1=sigma_D <= sigma_bg=sigma_2), the middle term of (3.1) is >=0 by the paper's own monotonicity Property 2.2, while the printed upper bound int_Omega (sigma_1-sigma_2)|grad u_2|^2 is <=0, so (3.1) forces the middle term to be <=0, which is false. Concrete counterexample: unit disk, sigma_1=1/2 on {r<1/2}, sigma_2=1, g=cos(theta): explicit solution gives <(Lambda_1-Lambda_2)g,g>=2pi/11, whereas the printed upper bound equals -pi/8. The correct standard inequality in terms of u_2 is int(sigma_2-sigma_1)|grad u_2|^2 <= <(Lambda_1-Lambda_2)g,g> <= int (sigma_2/sigma_1)(sigma_2-sigma_1)|grad u_2|^2 (equivalently, the middle term of the printed display should have the opposite sign); this correct version is exactly what the paper itself states at the start of Section 6. As printed, (3.1)'s lower bound is nonpositive in this regime, so the nonnegative lower bound in (3.2) cannot follow from the printed (3.1); (3.2) itself is nonetheless correct via the standard inequality, so the lemma's conclusion stands.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (3.1) with the correct two-sided inequality (flip the sign of its middle term, or state int(sigma_2-sigma_1)|grad u_2|^2 <= <(Lambda_1-Lambda_2)g,g> <= int (sigma_2/sigma_1)(sigma_2-sigma_1)|grad u_2|^2, as done in Section 6); the remainder of the proof is then valid unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The foundational recalled inequality in the proof of Lemma 3.1 is false as written and the displayed inference to (3.2) is broken as written; the lemma's conclusion, and hence the Kernel Method built on it, is unaffected once the standard correct inequality is used.
issues.title: The recalled two-sided monotonicity inequality (3.1) is false as printed, and the step deriving (3.2) from it is invalid as written
issues.why_classification: A single forced correction to a standard inequality, which the paper itself states correctly later, repairs both the display and the inference; no conclusion, method, or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega$ be a connected open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $n = 2,3$, and $A\subset\Omega$
Indeed, if $u_{bg}$ is constant in $D$, then it results to be constant over $\Omega$ and, consequently, on $\partial \Omega$.

issues.failure_explanation: A is allowed to be an arbitrary subset of Omega. If A is a null set (e.g., a singleton or the empty set), 'u constant in A' is vacuous or ill-defined for an H^1 function, and the conclusion is false: e.g., sigma=1, u(x)=x_1 on a disk is a nonconstant harmonic function that is constant on any singleton. The statement needs A to have nonempty interior (or positive Lebesgue measure, as in weak-UCP results of Alessandrini type for n=2 with L^infty coefficients and of Garofalo-Lin type for Lipschitz coefficients in n=3).

failure_location.quote: If $u$ is constant in $A$, then $u$ is constant in $\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that A has nonempty interior (equivalently |A|>0); no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The recalled Theorem 3.2 is false as stated; its application in the paper, where A=D is the open anomaly region, is unaffected.
issues.title: Weak UCP theorem stated with no hypothesis on the set A
issues.why_classification: A standard omitted hypothesis whose addition is a one-line local fix; the theorem's use in the paper and all downstream claims are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion |tilde lambda_k - lambda_k| <= ||N||_2 for eigenvalues ordered in decreasing order is Weyl's perturbation inequality, which requires the perturbation N to be self-adjoint (and compact), so that Lambda_n is self-adjoint with real eigenvalues. The source assumes only that N is a bounded operator; for a non-self-adjoint bounded N the eigenvalues of Lambda_n need not be real and the ordered-eigenvalue statement is not valid as written. The paper's own discrete noise model symmetrizes the perturbation (N=(A+A^T)/2), indicating the intended hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that N is self-adjoint (and compact), consistent with the symmetrized discrete noise model used in Section 7.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 6.1 is unsupported as stated; the subsequent noise-plateau discussion and the eigenvalue-selection criterion that cite it are unaffected once N is taken self-adjoint.
issues.title: Eigenvalue perturbation bound (Weyl) stated for a general bounded noise operator without self-adjointness
issues.why_classification: A standard omitted hypothesis with a one-line fix already reflected in the paper's numerical noise model; no result or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: To extract a lower bound on int_D sigma_bg|grad u_bg|^2 from the (correct) starting inequality F := <(Lambda_sigma_D - Lambda_bg)g,g> <= int_D (sigma_bg/sigma_a)(sigma_bg-sigma_a)|grad u_bg|^2, one needs an upper bound on (sigma_bg-sigma_a)/sigma_a, i.e. the constant (sigma_bg^M - sigma_a^m)/sigma_a^m. The paper instead divides by Delta_sigma = sigma_bg^m - sigma_a^M, which is a LOWER bound on the contrast, yielding the stronger, unjustified lower bound (sigma_a^m/Delta_sigma) F <= int_D sigma_bg|grad u_bg|^2. Counterexample: unit disk, sigma_bg = 10 for r<0.6 and 1 for 0.6<r<1, D = {r<0.3} with sigma_a = 0.5, g = cos(theta); the explicit piecewise-radial solution gives F = 0.04045 pi while int_D sigma_bg|grad u_bg|^2 = 0.01775 pi < (sigma_a^m/Delta_sigma) F = F. Thus the lower bound of (6.2) is false in the stated generality; it is valid only when sigma_bg^M - sigma_a^m = Delta_sigma, e.g., for uniform conductivities. The upper bound of (6.2) is correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the left endpoint by sigma_a^m/(sigma_bg^M - sigma_a^m) (derived from the same starting inequality with the maximal contrast), keep the correct right endpoint sigma_bg^M/Delta_sigma, and adjust the alpha=1 condition in the remark accordingly (for uniform sigma_a it becomes sigma_bg^M > 2 sigma_a); alternatively restrict the claim to piecewise-uniform conductivities.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised 'clear bounds for admissible values of epsilon', namely the interval alpha in (sigma_a^m/Delta_sigma, sigma_bg^M/Delta_sigma) in (6.4), has a wrong left endpoint for variable background or anomaly conductivities, and the subsequent justification of the alpha=1 threshold choice (the condition sigma_bg^m > sigma_a^m + sigma_a^M) inherits the error. For uniform conductivities (all numerical examples) the stated formulas coincide with the corrected ones, so the algorithm and examples are unaffected.
issues.title: Lower bound of (6.2) uses the minimal contrast Delta_sigma where the derivation requires the maximal contrast; the bound is false for non-uniform conductivities
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained one-line constant correction needing no new proof architecture, and the threshold methodology, algorithm, and all examples survive; but a stated quantitative guarantee is false in the general regime and must be replaced by a weaker, different bound, so it exceeds a minor local fix.
